authoring: Direct conversational authorship and cross-group comparison; no external LLM API or generated prose script.
scope_convention: Named primary passages were retrieved. Theory, atomistic simulation, macroscopic experiment and failed access are not conflated.

evidence.read: DeSalvo et al. original three-page 1992 paper, author-institution copy: page 28 explanation and coupled equations 1-4; page 29 equations 6-7 approximation and Figure 2; page 30 direct electronic Kerr contribution.
evidence.support: Off-phase-matched second-harmonic generation returns some light to the fundamental with a changed phase. Eliminating the generated field produces a Kerr-like low-conversion response. The experiment tunes the sign through phase mismatch; a separately measured electronic Kerr contribution remains positive.
evidence.limitation: The effective intensity-linear coefficient fails for large phase distortion. The paper's crystal-specific numerical coefficients and irradiance values are not generalized. Ordinary third-harmonic cascading is not counted separately.

parent_source_check.read: Moroney et al. 2022 original Results, equation 1 and paragraphs immediately after it.
parent_source_check.support: The existing Kerr source explicitly uses a direct third-order medium and calls its mechanism a nonresonant electronic response. Existing nonlinear-frequency-conversion card describes generation, not the phase-shifted return path.

evidence.read: Nagai et al. 2023 original manuscript: Introduction on internal/perpendicular degrees of freedom; Atomic Structure and Phasons and Discussion: Origin of Al diffusion, pages 3-5; equation 1 and Summary.
evidence.support: Calculated Al trajectories in approximants follow restricted sites represented by hyperatomic fluctuations. A sequence of site changes supplies diffusion without creating vacancies. The quasicrystal's internal phason coordinate is distinct from ordinary physical translation; a diffusive collective mode is discussed.
evidence.limitation: Heat capacity was measured experimentally, whereas the atom trajectories were simulated. Extension from approximants to quasicrystals and the anomalous-heat-capacity interpretation are model-dependent. The card makes no universal heat-capacity prediction or literal physical six-dimensional-space claim.

supplement.title: Dynamics of particle flips in two-dimensional quasicrystals
supplement.read: Engel et al. 2010 original simulation, Introduction; Section II.D local tiling description; Section VI conclusions.
supplement.quote: local scale, phason flips strongly resemble
supplement.support: Describes near-degenerate configurations, geometrically allowed flips and thermally activated long-time diffusion. Explicitly compares local flips to slow beta relaxation in glasses. Novelty is therefore assigned to the internal quasiperiodic structural degree, not to thermal hopping alone.

evidence.nearest_comparison: Stress-biased amorphous shear events, low-temperature tunneling phonon scatterers, unequal-species vacancy flow and stress-directed creep are existing cards. None currently identifies quasiperiodic internal configuration changes. This boundary remains explicit for parent review.
evidence.additional_retrieval: Francoual et al. 2003 PRL 91,225501 primary publisher search abstract describes wavelength-squared decay times of phason speckles; APS full text failed, so it is not represented as a directly read paper body.

evidence.read: Ratzinger and Wang revised original manuscript dated April 2024: Section II.A/B pages 2-3 assumptions 3-7, discussion pages 4-5 and equations 8-10. The first arXiv submission was 2022; the card identifies the read revision.
evidence.quote: leave the skin layer between two collisions
evidence.support: Long electron flights out of the thin driven region reduce RF conductivity relative to a DC-based local calculation. The authors compare a geometric surface-resistance model with measurements and established transport theory.
evidence.limitation: The equivalent uniform layer is a surface-resistance approximation, not a full complex impedance solution. It assumes a simple Fermi surface and small frequency-times-collision-time; surface scattering and extremely low-temperature small-angle events change accuracy. No universal frequency cutoff or numerical loss factor is copied.

historical_source.title: Reuter and Sondheimer · Theory of the Anomalous Skin Effect in Metals (1948)
historical_source.support: Publisher search abstract explicitly states failure of local Ohm response when free path becomes comparable to field penetration depth. Direct page request failed; no original body read is claimed.

evidence.nearest_comparison: Induction/heating/sensing describe induced currents and their uses; this resolves finite-flight nonlocal response. Ballistic quantization counts transverse modes. Knudsen gas transport is controlled by pore-wall collisions rather than leaving a shallow electromagnetic drive layer.

exclusions.reason: Exact existing negative co-rotating frequency and absorptive sign-reversal mechanism.
Exact existing finite-beam angular-spectrum phase-gradient pathway.
